question.text: Following the SEBI (AIF) (Amendment) Regulations, 2024, the requirement to appoint a SEBI-registered custodian is:

answer.text: Compulsory for the Sponsor or Manager of ALL AIFs (all categories) for safekeeping of securities.
Applicable only to Category III AIFs that use leverage.
Required only if the corpus exceeds INR 500 crore.
Optional if all securities are held in dematerialised form with a depository.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per SEBI (AIF) (Amendment) Regulations, 2024 (w.e.f. January 5, 2024), the Sponsor or Manager of an AIF shall COMPULSORILY appoint a custodian registered with SEBI for safekeeping of securities — for ALL categories of AIFs. For Category III AIFs, the custodian additionally keeps custody of securities and goods received against physical settlement of commodity derivatives. The custodian must be appointed BEFORE the first investment of the scheme. The Trap: Option B reflects the pre-2024 partial rule. Option C invents a corpus threshold. Option D confuses demat holding with the custodial safekeeping mandate — they are separate requirements. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C and XIX-D both test the post-2024 universal custodian rule. XXI-B (PM) has a separate custodian rule under PM Regulations. VIII (Derivatives) touches custodial settlement of exchange-traded instruments. Manager's Pro-Tip: Appoint your custodian BEFORE first investment, not after. SEBI Circular Jan 12, 2024 requires custodian-in-place as a condition precedent to first drawdown deployment. The related-party carve-out (Reg 20) needs specific conditions met — don't default to your sponsor's group custodian without running the related-party test.
